subject: Customer DPA: Meditech — initial redlines and counsel questions
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Jane Lawrence <jane.lawrence@meditech.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Redwood DPA + subprocessor list — starting redlines

Hi Jane,

Thanks again for the time on Friday — attaching our standard DPA (Redwood_Standard_DPA_v2.docx) and the current subprocessor inventory link. To keep things moving, can your counsel flag any high-level non-starters up front (SCCs vs EU-US addendum preference, mandatory audit right scope, data retention caps)?

Quick context / asks:
- We propose standard 30-day notice for new subprocessors with an opt-out right for Meditech for processors that present material risk. If counsel prefers a longer notice window, let us know suggested language.
- For international transfers, we typically use the EU SCCs + EU-US Addendum where applicable. If you require an alternate legal basis, please list.
- We can provide SOC 2 Type II and an extract of our subprocessor risk assessments — attaching the SOC 2 report separately.

Attachments: Redwood_Standard_DPA_v2.docx, link to subprocessor inventory (Drive).

I’ll coordinate with our legal (Neha) and sales ops (Karthik) once we get your redlines. If you prefer DocuSign for countersignature at the end, we’ll kick that off from our side.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0183

Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference platform.
From: Jane Lawrence <jane.lawrence@meditech.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Meditech Legal <legal@meditech.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@meditech.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 09:10:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA + subprocessor list — starting redlines

Ava,

Thanks for the materials. Please see attached initial redlines (Meditech_DPA_Redlines_20271202.pdf) from our outside counsel. High-level questions and comments:

1) Subprocessors — request 45 days' notice and a specific right to object if the subprocessor will process personal data for Meditech’s EHR-related workflows.
2) Audit rights — counsel is asking to clarify scope: need to ensure we have the ability to obtain audit reports and, in narrow cases, to conduct on-site audits. Would you accept a scoped audit right limited to incidents or material changes?
3) Data transfers — counsel prefers an explicit EU-US Addendum with SCCs called out in the DPA text. Also seeking confirmation on transfer impact if a subprocessor is in a high-risk jurisdiction.
4) Retention — they want maximum retention periods for logs and processed outputs (they suggested 13 months for user logs).
5) Encryption & KMS — request optional covenant that keys for certain production tenants be customer-managed (KMS/HSM) for PHI-like data.

We are aiming for a commercial close the week of Dec 13 — procurement will need a countersigned DPA and PO by then to hit internal timelines.

Regards,
Jane Lawrence
Sr. Counsel — Privacy & Contracts
Meditech Health

---
Attachment: Meditech_DPA_Redlines_20271202.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jane Lawrence <jane.lawrence@meditech.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Dec 2027 11:04:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Redwood DPA + subprocessor list — starting redlines

Jane — thanks for the thorough notes. Quick internal responses and proposed edits attached (Redwood_DPA_Tracked_20271204.docx). Summary of positions: 

- Notice period: we can accept 45 days for subprocessor onboarding for EHR/PHI-scoped processing only. For general-purpose subprocessors we ask for 30 days. Draft language in tracked copy distinguishes the two cases.
- Audit rights: we can agree to scoped audit rights limited to (i) incidents that materially affect Meditech data, (ii) third-party certifications (SOC2), and (iii) random audit right subject to reasonable limitations and NDA. On-site audits: available only for material incidents and must be pre-scheduled with reasonable notice.
- Transfers: we'll incorporate explicit reference to the EU SCCs and include an EU-US Addendum clause. If a subprocessor operates in a jurisdiction counsel deems high risk, we will either (a) offer supplementary safeguards or (b) engage in mitigations (pseudonymization, contractual constraints).
- KMS/customer keys: for workloads containing regulated data we can offer a customer-managed KMS option on dedicated deployments (Dedicated or Private plans). For hosted customers we provide HSM-backed key management and can provide attestation.

We aim to produce a redline that is actionable for your counsel — attached tracked changes. If Meditech can identify the subset of workloads that require customer-managed keys, we’ll draft the KMS annex.

Next step: Ava — I’ll need a quick confirmation on whether procurement needs the DocuSign envelope immediately or after legal signoff. If legal is comfortable, we can send a DocuSign envelope for countersignature and loop in procurement.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Tracked_20271204.docx
From: Jane Lawrence <jane.lawrence@meditech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@redwood.com>, Meditech Legal <legal@meditech.com>, procurement@meditech.com
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2027 10:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA + subprocessor list — starting redlines

Karthik/Ava,

Appreciate the callout on KMS and the tracked language. A few operational follow-ups from our security team: 

- Can Redwood provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report via secure link and the date of the last penetration test?
- We need a short summary of the subprocessor risk assessment process (frequency, criteria for decommissioning).
- On retention: our teams want a firm maximum for user activity logs and processed outputs. Are you flexible with 13 months for logs and 90 days for model outputs derived from Meditech patient data?

Also — procurement reiterated the timeline: countersigned DPA + PO by Dec 13 to meet go-live on Jan 3. If legal needs extra time, please surface the blockers by EOD Dec 8 so we can escalate internally.

Thanks,
Jane

---
Meditech Procurement copied for visibility.
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Jane Lawrence <jane.lawrence@meditech.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2027 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Redwood DPA + subprocessor list — starting redlines

Jane — quick update and links to the requested artifacts:

- SOC 2 Type II report: available here (SOC2_Report_Redwood_2027.pdf) — link shared via secure portal.
- Pen test: most recent external penetration test completed 2027-08-14; summary attached in the portal.
- Subprocessor risk assessment: we perform continuous monitoring with quarterly formal reviews; decommissioning criteria and escalation process summarized here: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/meditech/dpa-subproc-inventory (see tab ‘Risk & Decommission’).
- Retention: we can accept 13 months for user activity logs and 90 days for model output retention when the outputs contain identifiable Meditech patient data. We’ll add explicit retention caps to Section 4.2 in the tracked DPA.
- KMS: for the production tenants you identify as regulated, we’ll prepare a KMS annex; this will require a Dedicated or Private deployment (can go in the SoW).

DocuSign status: I’ve created the envelope and will only send it once counsel confirms the final tracked copy. DocuSign envelope draft: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/ABC123def456

Next asks: Jane — if you can confirm the subset of workloads requiring customer-managed keys and confirm whether Meditech is happy with the scoped audit right language in the attached tracked DPA, we’ll prepare final copy for countersignature. Procurement — please confirm expected PO date relative to Dec 13 (we can accept an LOE if PO timing slips).

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com
